chapter: Postwar years, accident and lean times
title: Back in New York in the 1950s: lost contacts, jazz giving way to rock
summary: After years away he found gigs scarce, since people forget a man who is out of town, and rock was displacing jazz.

story.theme_name: Where jazz stands today: young players, rock, and the audience
story.community_name: Is jazz healthy? Young players, rock and the future

blocks.x: Came back here. Now, you're back in New York, and we're into what? We're into the 1950's, and we're back in sort of the same situation you were into several years before, the potential of gigging around, but also the kind of jazz you were playing was no longer just the only kind of jazz around. There were very --
No, I start going to -- yeah, you're
right. Because they started going into rock stuff, and that kind of --
That -- you're now into almost the rock period. Did you -- did -- having been away for so long, from New York, did you have trouble getting gigs?
Yes, because once you lose contact, you know --

Because a guy'd come up to you and say Hey, Herman, what are you doing tonight? You know, when they get so they can't do that. You call up one, say oh, he's out of town. You (smack) -- next time something comes up he says well this guy's -- somebody told me he's out of town. I'll call somebody I know's in town, because I don't have time to waste, you know, checking on -- I'd like to have him, but I don't have the time to be -- you know.

So now was this -- was this period, then, a worse period for you than right after the war when you came back from Philadelphia? That you said was a bad period. But now you've been away, and the situation has changed a bit.

I would say -- well I would say it was worse. I'll tell you why, why I say that. Because the trends -- the changing trend from jazz to rock, and you don't have as many jobs of jazz as we had before, becuase people
are doing one thing or the other, and if you don't have a banjo and some [Tin Pan] (unintelligible) Bang-a-ding-a-ding-a-bang -- you don't work, and you don't eat. You know.

And I was doing it, so you don't go into that, so you don't -- those guys, you turn around and read a paper, and hear where this guy's making thousands, and you're not make $15.00 a week. You know what I mean? There's your answer, you know?
